correctness.rationale: An arbitrary extension is represented by an L∞ vector kernel; moment constraints yield exact trace n. Pointwise Holder proves sharp n^(1/p) norm and unique equality for p>1. A constructive parameter interval establishes p=1 nonuniqueness. Haagerup p=1 constant, interpolation and two-coordinate equality give exact Q norms for p>=2. Permutation symmetrization proves p=1 exact norm. Explicit moment-preserving orthogonal perturbations attain the Hilbert stability inequality for every C>=sqrt(n). Finite experiments are diagnostics, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Compared exact minimal extension norm and equality/fiber classifications, not just title or exponent. The motivating 2026 text gives a POE-p iff order continuity theorem and an earlier qualitative Rademacher counterexample; it does not establish the finite n coefficient probe costs, uniqueness of all minimum-norm extensions, or the exact Hilbert stability identity. Haagerup determines the scalar Khintchine constant, not vector-valued minimal extension fibers; Lewicki-Micek studies L1-valued Fourier-type minimal extensions with different codomain geometry. Equivalent older Fourier terminology remains a substantive residual risk.

value.rationale: Rademacher L1 is a canonical obstruction to the recent POE-p characterization. Exact relative finite extension factors show sharp-order growth at all finite p and give full formulas at the endpoint and at p>=2; the unique/minimizer classification identifies a strict target-geometry transition, and the globally sharp L2 stability quantifies the rigid optimal extension. These naturally measured constants and equality cases are distinct from the known qualitative obstruction and from a routine arbitrary slice.
